newsitem.title: UK: Reinstated Wickes dropped from FTSE-250.
newsitem.headline: Reinstated Wickes dropped from FTSE-250.

text.p: Britain's FTSE International said on Tuesday its actuaries' indices committee had approved the removal of do-it-yourself retail group Wickes Plc from the FTSE 250 index after a seven month suspension ended.
The share was reinstated after shareholders approved a 53 million stg rescue rights issue and capital restructuring.
In a brief statement, FTSE International said Wickes would be included in the FTSE SmallCap index after the close of business on Tuesday.
The transfer, it explained, was made in accordance with rules governing the treatment of reinstated constituents.

On its return on Tuesday, Wickes shares set an expected premium to the 150p price of the firm's rights issue, supported by speculation of a bid from a retailer such as Kingfisher Plc or building materials group such as RMC Plc.
From a peak after the opening of about 211 pence, the shares ended at 195-1/2p, with volume reaching 3.14 million shares.
Detailing its restructuring plans last December, Wickes said last December that 150p price of the new shares being issued in its rights issue was equivalent to 15p per existing share.
Analysts said that meant today's share trade left Wickes shares at less than 20 pence under the former valuation basis.
Wickes shares were suspended at 69p last June after the discovery of accounting irregularities which had inflated its profits.
Last November the company appointed Bill Grimsey as its new chief executive, following the departure of former chairman and chief executive Henry Sweetbaum.
Four former senior managers of the company are under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office.
